name: The Moravian Square Oak

location.address: Moravské náměstí (park), near the fountain, Brno-střed

verified_sources: AOPK CR pamatne stromy register (data/registers/czech-aopk-pamatne-stromy.json, kod 101079, CC BY 4.0)
access: Free, public park square in the city centre
transport: Roughly 15 minutes on foot from Brno hlavní nádraží (the main train station)
verify_notes: Czech name: Dub letní na Moravském náměstí (register kod 101079, isop_id 44659). Grows in the park on Moravské náměstí, part of the ring of parks that replaced Brno's city walls after they were demolished 1809-1859. Declared a memorial tree 27 June 1985 by the Brno National Committee together with two other trees (one of them is brq_002 below); reason given was that it was the strongest tree in the park and a significant solitary specimen. Already valued at over 600,000 Kčs at the time of designation. Widely called the most beautiful memorial oak in the city of Brno (turistika.cz). Height just under 30m. Girth 435cm as of the most recent measurement cited by turistika.cz/city sources; the AOPK national register (last changed 2024-06-16) lists 440cm, essentially the same figure, so no real conflict, just rounding/measurement-year drift. Pruned of some dead branches around 2005 and reported in very good health since. FLAG REASON: no single dated post-2020 photo or news item found this pass confirming it standing today, though the AOPK register record itself was last verified/updated 2024-06-16 (kept publishable=true, i.e. not one of the register's own confirmed-gone entries) and Wikimedia Commons carries photos of this exact tree uploaded in 2026. Treat as good but not exhaustively current.

name: The Old Town Gate Oak

location.address: Moravské náměstí (south end of the park), Brno-střed

verified_sources: AOPK CR pamatne stromy register (data/registers/czech-aopk-pamatne-stromy.json, kod 106252, CC BY 4.0)
access: Free, public park square in the city centre
transport: Roughly 15 minutes on foot from Brno hlavní nádraží (the main train station)
verify_notes: Czech name: Dub u vstupu na Moravské náměstí (register kod 106252, isop_id 56771). Stands at the southern tip of the same Moravské náměstí park as brq_001, roughly 130m away and clearly distinguishable from it (a second, separately named and separately protected oak, not a register twin). Planted in the ring park that grew up after the demolition of Brno's fortifications (1809-1859), close to where the Tišnov Gate (Tišnovská brána) once stood, now long gone. City-encyclopedia record (Encyklopedie dějin Brna, the municipal/university heritage encyclopedia): height 25m, age given as '170+ years', girth measured 410cm in 2004 and 423cm in 2010. Protection zone is a 13.4m-radius circle around the trunk in which no tree-damaging activity is permitted. AOPK register (kod 106252) gives a newer girth of 480cm; last register update recorded 2018-03-02, older than most of this cluster's other entries. FLAG REASON: freshest photo evidence found this pass for this specific tree (as opposed to its neighbour) is from the city encyclopedia, dated 3 May 2015; no Wikimedia Commons category or more recent sighting turned up in the time available. Deliver as good but ask a reader to confirm on a future visit.

name: The Horse Chestnut of Rooseveltova

location.address: Park Danuše Muzikářové, Rooseveltova, opposite the Janáček Theatre

verified_sources: AOPK CR pamatne stromy register (data/registers/czech-aopk-pamatne-stromy.json, kod 105037, CC BY 4.0)
transport: Roughly 12 minutes on foot from Brno hlavní nádraží (the main train station); adjacent to the Janáček Theatre
verify_notes: Czech name: Jírovec maďal na Rooseveltově / na Roosveltově ulici (register kod 105037, isop_id 53643). Stands in the central part of the small park on Rooseveltova street, opposite the Janáček Theatre, near the former Governor's/Viceroy's Palace (Místodržitelský palác); a surviving piece of the first historical redesign of this ground after Brno's fortifications came down. Declared a memorial tree in 2007. Girth 320-326cm at 130cm above ground depending on source (register: 326cm; turistika-derived figure: 320cm); height about 25m. An archiweb.cz architecture-news piece (about underground garage construction nearby raising concern for the tree's roots) independently corroborates the tree's existence, species, protected status and exact park. Park itself was renamed Park Danuše Muzikářové in 2019. Wikimedia Commons carries photographs of this exact tree uploaded as recently as April 2026, good current-standing evidence.

name: The Plane Tree Below Petrov

location.address: Terrace on the old ramparts, end of Denisovy sady park, below Petrov Cathedral

verified_sources: AOPK CR pamatne stromy register (data/registers/czech-aopk-pamatne-stromy.json, kod 101080, CC BY 4.0)
access: Free, public park. Honest caveat: the small terrace immediately around the tree is closed to visitors in winter, open in the tourist season
transport: Roughly 10 minutes on foot from Brno hlavní nádraží (the main train station); inside Denisovy sady, near Zelný trh (the Cabbage Market)
verify_notes: Czech name: Platan javorolistý na Petrově, also called Platan pod Petrovem (register kod 101080, isop_id 44660). Grows on the old city ramparts at the end of Denisovy sady park, right below the Cathedral of St Peter and Paul on Petrov hill, one of Brno's most recognisable landmarks. Crown reaches about 25m, girth 415cm per turistika.cz (register gives 400cm, essentially the same). Age estimated at 160 years. The small terrace the tree stands on is kept planted with flower displays through the tourist season and is closed off in winter, a real access caveat worth stating plainly rather than glossing over. Regarded locally as one of the most striking corners of Denisovy sady. Wikimedia Commons category holds photographs of this specific tree, most recently uploaded February 2026.

name: The Plane Tree of St Anne's

location.address: Grounds of St Anne's University Hospital (Fakultní nemocnice u sv. Anny), Pekařská, between pavilions V and C1

verified_sources: AOPK CR pamatne stromy register (data/registers/czech-aopk-pamatne-stromy.json, kod 101082, CC BY 4.0)
access: Within the grounds of a public teaching hospital, not a private clinic. Enter through the gate on the south side, off Hybešova street; the hospital campus is open on foot during the day without needing to state hospital business, but the tree is not in an ordinary park, so say so plainly on the page
transport: Roughly 15-20 minutes on foot from Brno hlavní nádraží (the main train station), or a short walk from the Mendlovo náměstí tram/bus interchange
verify_notes: Czech name: Platan U sv. Anny (register kod 101082, isop_id 44662). Stands inside the grounds of St Anne's University Hospital, one of Brno's major teaching hospitals, between pavilions V and C1 off Pekařská street; turistika.cz names the south gate from Hybešova street as the easiest approach. Girth given as 565cm (turistika.cz, hospital's own likely source) versus 575cm in the AOPK register, essentially the same tree measured a little later. Canopy reached almost 40m before the crown was trimmed (measured 2004); the trunk branches into several secondary stems around 4m up. Sources speculate, without stating it as fact, that the tree may date to the same period as the hospital building itself, built 1865-68 in Neo-Renaissance style by the Viennese architect Theophil Hansen, which would put it at over 150 years; treat that link as plausible rather than proven, and phrase the story that way. FLAG REASON: this is hospital-campus, not park, land; the access line above states that honestly rather than presenting it as an ordinary public park, per the loosened access rule (a hospital garden with a walk-in gate is a yes, but must be described honestly).

name: The Plane Tree of Benešova

location.address: Corner of Benešova and Divadelní streets, by the site of the former Brno bus station
location.neighbourhood: Brno-střed (city centre, near the main train station)

verified_sources: AOPK CR pamatne stromy register (data/registers/czech-aopk-pamatne-stromy.json, kod 101081, CC BY 4.0)
transport: Roughly 5 minutes on foot from Brno hlavní nádraží (the main train station)
verify_notes: Czech name: Platan javorolistý na Benešově, also labelled na Divadelní on Wikimedia Commons (register kod 101081, isop_id 44661). Stands at the corner of Benešova and Divadelní streets, at the site of Brno's former bus station (Autobusové nádraží u hotelu Grand), a 1948-49 modernist building designed by architect Bohuslav Fuchs; a nice detail for the story if the writer wants it, since the tree has outlasted the building's original use. City-encyclopedia street profile confirms the address as Benešova 0/01 (a '0' house number in Czech addressing typically marks a plot rather than a numbered building, consistent with a street-corner tree on public land). Girth: AOPK register gives 368cm; the Czech Wikipedia list gives 310cm at the same coordinates, an older or differently-dated measurement, not a contradiction, just growth over time; state the register's more recent figure. No age estimate found in any source this pass; leave it empty rather than guess, per the honesty rule. No species dispute. Least remarkable-looking of this cluster on paper (a street tree at a road junction rather than a park specimen) but genuinely public, genuinely verified, and it completes a compact city-centre walk alongside the other five.
